text:
Rebecca (support): Hey team, customer #8421 opened an escalation — large p99 latency spike (~8-12s) for /v1/generate after today's runtime rollout (v2026.03.17-rc2). No 5xxs, just long tails and some client timeouts. Asking for mitigation asap.

deploy-bot: rollout completed to prod-us-west at 2026-03-17T12:15:22Z, commit=abc123def, changeset: enable_kv_prefetch=true, allocator=tcmalloc-2.1, kernel-selector=fast-path.

Maya (eng-runtime): Noted. Canary yesterday looked flat for the short window we sampled but our long-tail tests were limited.

Jordan (oncall): Grafana snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc/p99-overview?orgId=1&panelId=7 -> p99 jump aligns with replicas 7-9 in us-west-2, starting 12:16 UTC. Traces: https://traces/trace/0xdeadbeef show long queueing + a few 500-700ms handler GC pauses.

Sam (SRE): Looking at sidecar logs, I see RSS climb:
```
2026-03-17T12:16:59Z sidecar[pid=1234] INFO rss_mb=5120 alloc_delta_mb=420 prefetch=true request_id=xyz
2026-03-17T12:17:02Z sidecar[pid=1234] WARN gc_pause_ms=480 rss_mb=5376
```
Pattern: long-context requests trigger KV prefetch which allocs per-request buffers; with concurrency that pushes RSS over the tuned limit and we start to see OS reclaim/pauses.

Maya (eng-runtime): I pushed the KV prefetch feature behind a flag last week. Candidate root cause: prefetch buffer sizing + a subtle change in allocator (tcmalloc bump) -> higher RSS growth under bursty long-context workloads.

Rebecca (support): Customer repro: POSTs a ~8k-token prompt + function-call params, concurrency 20. They can reproduce reliably against prod using their key.

Jordan (oncall): Proposed immediate mitigations:
- roll back runtime in us-west to previous stable build (abc000) for prod traffic split 100% -> quick rollback to stop customer impact
- set per-replica concurrency cap to 6 for the affected pool
- temporarily disable kv_prefetch flag for runtime via remote config

Maya (eng-runtime): Agree. For long-term we should bisect to find the minimal change: candidates in range abc000..abc123 (notable PRs: #4018 allocator bump, #4023 kv-prefetch, #4027 batching tweak). I'll prepare a canary-bisect plan.

Sam (SRE): I'll run an automated bisect in staging. Plan: deploy each candidate commit to staging cluster, run our long-tail harness (1000 requests with 8k tokens at qps=30), collect RSS/GC/latency. If p99 > 2s or RSS > 4.5GB we mark commit as suspect.

Luis (infra): I can apply a temporary limit on container memory and enable OOM killer accounting to ensure a single replica doesn't destabilize the pool. Also enabling swap=off on those hosts to avoid swap-induced latencies.

Maya (eng-runtime): Quick hotfix: cap per-request prefetch buffer to 32MB and add early-fail if total_prefetch_inflight > 1GB. I can build a patch and cut a canary by 12:50 UTC.

Rebecca (support): Customer update: saying you're investigating and we'll apply a mitigation shortly. They asked if a rollback is possible; they're ok with a short downtime.

Jordan (oncall): Action items: 
- Sam: start staging bisect now and report earliest suspect commit (ETA 60m)
- Maya: prepare hotfix and canary (ETA 35m)
- Luis: apply per-replica mem cap + throttle (ETA 20m)
- Rebecca: keep customer updated; ask for request IDs if they repro again (sample IDs help).

Sam (SRE): Starting bisect now. Kicking off load jobs. Will post links to staging traces once they finish.

Maya (eng-runtime): Hotfix built and pushed to canary channel: build=abc124-hotfix, changes: prefetch_cap=32MB, prefetch_inflight_limit=1GB. Canaries deployed to canary pool at 12:38 UTC.

Jordan (oncall): Early canary results: p99 back to baseline on canary pool after hotfix, RSS stays under 4GB for long-context runs. Staging bisect still running to isolate commit.

Sam (SRE): Bisect result (preliminary): PR #4023 (kv-prefetch) is the earliest commit that reproduces the RSS growth in staging. #4018 (allocator) amplifies it but doesn't reproduce alone. Marking #4023 as root cause candidate.

Maya (eng-runtime): Thanks. Plan: revert #4023 from prod (or disable via feature flag) and keep allocator bump for other perf improvements. We'll roll the revert to us-west by 13:20 UTC.

Jordan (oncall): Rolling revert now for prod us-west traffic (traffic-split->stable-abc000). Monitoring p95/p99.

deploy-bot: rollback to commit=abc000 started at 2026-03-17T13:10:02Z.

Rebecca (support): Customer confirmed latency returned to normal after ~10 minutes post-rollback. They're marking as resolved for now but want a postmortem.

Maya (eng-runtime): Postmortem notes to capture: root cause = aggressive kv_prefetch buffers combined with allocator change -> memory pressure -> GC/OS-level pauses -> p99 regressions; mitigations = revert/feature-flag, prefetch caps, mem caps, improved canary long-tail tests.

Sam (SRE): Follow-ups: add long-tail nightly canary tests, add RSS and prefetch_inflight alert rule (pager at 5GB or 75% of container limit), and automated bisect tooling docs.

Luis (infra): I'll add a temporary runbook for memory-pressure rollbacks and enable container-level oom_score_adj tuning for the pool.

Rebecca (support): I'll coordinate the customer PM for a follow-up call and share the timeline.

Maya (eng-runtime): I'll open a follow-up PR to reintroduce prefetch in a safer mode (adaptive caps) and add unit tests covering buffer accounting.

Jordan (oncall): Closing triage for now; will reopen if we see any regressions after staging re-deploys. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
